sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2004. Rapid appraisal sociolinguistic research of Dugwor. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2004-009. 18 pp.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2001. Rapid appraisal sociolinguistic research of Dugwor: ALCAM [162] (Diamaré Division, Far North Province). Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research. 16 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47246)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (Feb 2000) with two 120-item Dougour/Mikiri wordlists in Appendix 1 (forms carry acute accents, unexplained, e.g. 'méy' mouth, 'ré' eye); the only phonology remark is 'There is no phonology. Any writing of the language is being done by those who attended school and are applying what they learned there.' (p. 8, §3.5.2, the scanned text). No word on stress, tone or accent.

sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)

sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification source (p. 68); comparative wordlist work on the Mofu/Mafa group that may note whether the Dugwor data were tone-marked, but will not give a stress rule.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The Reconstruction of the Phonology and Lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the Linguistic History of the Central Chadic Languages. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT. 437 pp. ISBN 978-94-6093-157-4.

tone.quote: The result is a reconstruction of the sound system of Proto-Central Chadic (though not including tone or stress), and of the daughter languages of Proto-Central Chadic ... Studies in the development of Central Chadic tone systems are at a very early stage. ... For Zulgo (Haller 1980), Gemzek (Gravina 2003), Merey (Gravina) and Dugwor (Ousmanou 1999) both palatalization and labialization prosodies are present. ... Dugwor neutralises vowels in the antepenultimate syllable to /ə/
tone.locator: p. 3 (ch. 1 Introduction) for 'though not including tone or stress'; p. 86 for the tone-systems sentence; p. 97 (ch. 'Vowel Prosody') for the Zulgo/Gemzek/Merey/Dugwor prosodies sentence; p. 103 for 'Dugwor neutralises vowels..'
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
